newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev ends touch softer at 498-500 vs dlr.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev ends touch softer at 498-500 vs dlr.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 498-500 per dollar, a touch softer than 495-496 at the opening due to longer value date and a slight rise in foreign currency demand, dealers said.
"The lev slide was mainly due to the longer value date of spot deals. A small rise in dollar demand from an energy importer also put some pressure on the lev," a commercial bank dealer said.
Final clients and the central bank were seen buying dollars around 491-495 levs with settlement date on December 30, traders said. @
Central bank officials were not available for comment.
The value date of today's spot deals is January 3. Markets in Bulgaria will be closed from December 31 through January 2 for the New Year.
The current large spread between interest rates on lev- and dollar-denominated deposits allows for a daily lev depreciation by around two levs against the dollar, dealers said.
Central bank main interest rate is now set at 15 percent monthly or 180 percent annually. @
The Socialist government resignation was not expected to cause a sharp lev fall in the next few days but could prompt a lev decline at the beginning of next year, dealers said.

"A rise in dollar demand from large final clients may strongly pressure the lev in the first days of January as banks will be reluctant to pare forex positions amid uncertainty about the future government," another dealer said.
Bulgaria's parliament today approved Prime Minister's Zhan Videnov resignation tendered at a party congress a week ago. @

Under fire for his handling of a severe economic crisis, Videnov resigned last Saturday, saying he felt he lacked the support he needed from the party and the country to continue as prime minister and party leader.

According to the constitution, Videnov's cabinet remains in power until the ruling Bulgarian Socialist Party forms a new cabinet which should be approved by parliament next month. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-876032
